title: RBAC anomaly hunt & evidence-harvest procedures
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a field-operational runbook for hunt-style RBAC anomalies and the fast, forensically-sound extraction of audit/evidence required for SIEM ingestion and later postmortems. It focuses on:
 - rapid triage of suspicious role/permission changes,
 - automated and manual evidence-harvest procedures,
 - minimal-impact preservation, and
 - handoff to IR/postmortem owners.

Audience and scope:
Intended for on-call security engineers and SREs who must respond to anomalous permission events (unexpected admin grants, burst role creations, cross-account/service principal escalations). This is not the full incident management SOP (see IR runbooks), but a targeted playbook for RBAC-specific evidence capture and SIEM export steps.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
[ ] 1) Confirm alert source and severity. Note alert ID, timestamp, and short description.
[ ] 2) Identify actor (user/service) and target resource(s).
[ ] 3) If the actor is a human account, check recent authentications and MFA status.
[ ] 4) Freeze automated role-provisioning jobs if possible (e.g., disable Terraform/GitHub Actions runners).
[ ] 5) Begin evidence snapshot (see Preservation checklist).

Roles & responsibilities:
 - On-call Security Engineer: execute hunt queries, preserve evidence, document timeline.
 - Infra/SRE: assist with snapshots, temporary ACLs, and service restarts if needed.
 - Product/Platform Owner: advise on business impact and approve changes to production infra.
 - Legal/Compliance (if escalated): preserve broader communications and approve disclosure.

Detection heuristics (examples of RBAC anomalies to treat as high-priority):
 - >3 new admin role grants in <10 minutes to different principals.
 - Role bindings created outside of expected CI/CD windows.
 - Service principal bound to both internal and external projects simultaneously.
 - Unexpected change from low-privilege to high-privilege in a single session.
 - Permission drift events that coincide with unusual deployments.

SIEM / Audit extraction recipes (examples)
(Adapt for Splunk/Elastic/BigQuery/Cloud Logging as appropriate)
 - Cloud Logging (gcloud):
   gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName:GrantRole OR protoPayload.methodName:SetIamPolicy' --project=redwood-prod --freshness=7d --format=json > /tmp/rbac-grants-$(date +%s).json
 - BigQuery (if logs exported):
   SELECT * FROM `redwood-logs.audit_log_*` WHERE protoPayload.methodName LIKE '%SetIamPolicy%' AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY);
 - Elastic / Kibana DSL (example):
   {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"match": {"event.action": "set_iam_policy"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-7d"}}}]}}}
 - Generic SIEM search terms: "SetIamPolicy", "AddRoleBinding", "create_role", "grant_role", "permission:iam"

Preservation checklist (immediate):
1) Create a read-only snapshot of the audit stream for the suspect window. Naming: evidence/rbac/{alert-id}/{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}_audit.json
2) Copy snapshots to secure evidence bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/ or gs://redwood-evidence/) with ACLs limited to security and legal.
   - Example: aws s3 cp /tmp/rbac-grants-*.json s3://redwood-evidence/rbac/{alert-id}/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control --storage-class STANDARD
3) Export current IAM role bindings (live state) for all affected projects/accounts.
4) Freeze change pipelines: temporarily remove write permissions on IaC pipelines that could mutate bindings. Document who approved the freeze.
5) Record relevant ephemeral tokens or sessions (do not store plaintext secrets in the evidence bucket) — capture session IDs, timestamps, and correlation IDs.

Chain-of-custody note:
 - Always record the extractor, extraction timestamp, storage location, and checksum (sha256). Use the following filename manifest format in the evidence directory: manifest-{alert-id}.txt with lines: file,sha256,extracted_by,extracted_at

Automated evidence-harvest snippet (psuedo/ops playbook)
# minimal script sketch for investigators (adapt to environment)
ALERT_ID="SEC-XXXX"
WINDOW_START="2025-11-01T00:00:00Z"
WINDOW_END="2025-11-01T02:00:00Z"
OUT_DIR="/tmp/evidence/$ALERT_ID"
mkdir -p $OUT_DIR
# pull cloud audit logs (gcloud example)
gcloud logging read "timestamp>='$WINDOW_START' AND timestamp<='$WINDOW_END' AND (protoPayload.methodName:GrantRole OR protoPayload.methodName:SetIamPolicy)" --project=redwood-prod --format=json > $OUT_DIR/audit-window.json
sha256sum $OUT_DIR/audit-window.json > $OUT_DIR/audit-window.json.sha256
# upload
aws s3 cp $OUT_DIR s3://redwood-evidence/rbac/$ALERT_ID/ --recursive --acl bucket-owner-full-control
# write manifest
echo "audit-window.json,$(cut -d' ' -f1 $OUT_DIR/audit-window.json.sha256),$USER,$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > $OUT_DIR/manifest-$ALERT_ID.txt

Minimal SIEM export mapping (fields to include for downstream forensic logic)
 - timestamp
 - actor.principal (user/service)
 - actor.ip
 - resource.type
 - resource.name
 - action.method (e.g., SetIamPolicy, AddRoleBinding)
 - change.details (diff if available)
 - request_id / trace_id
 - session_id / token_id
 - cloud.project / account
 - checksum_of_exported_file

Escalation matrix (samples)
 - P1 (active lateral movement / mass escalations): Pager to Security Lead + SRE manager, immediate legal notification.
 - P2 (suspicious single-account elevation with unknown actor): On-call security + product security lead in 30 minutes.
 - P3 (informational / low risk): Documented and tracked in SEC backlog.

Post-incident handoff (what IR wants from evidence harvest)
 - Full audit snapshot for suspicious window (raw JSON), with SHA256.
 - Live state export of IAM bindings (CSV or JSON).
 - Timeline file (timestamps + explanatory notes for each action taken by responders).
 - Any correlated logs (build system runs, terraform apply runs, CI job logs) with links.
 - Short write-up (3–5 bullets) summarizing root cause hypothesis and next 3 remediation steps.

Postmortem template (to fill after containment):
 - Incident ID:
 - Detection vector (alert type + SIEM query):
 - Timeline (UTC): detection -> evidence preserved -> containment -> remediation -> close
 - Root cause (short):
 - Impact (systems/users/data):
 - Mitigation actions taken:
 - Remediation & long-term fixes (owners + due dates):
 - Lessons learned and monitoring changes:

Automations & future work (tech debt/backlog notes):
 - Add dedicated RBAC anomaly dashboard with pre-built hunt queries.
 - Automate evidence snapshotter as a serverless function (triggered by alert) to reduce time-to-preserve.
 - Add immutable retention policy for evidence buckets for at least 1 year with access logging.
 - Build an RBAC-diff tool that computes minimal permission delta between two snapshots.

Contacts (quick):
 - Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.ai (pager: +1-555-0101)
 - Platform SRE lead: evan.mckenzie@redwood.ai
 - Infra IAM SME: priya.shah@redwood.ai
 - Legal (incident response): legal-ir@redwood.ai

Notes and references:
 - This document is intentionally pragmatic and harvest-focused; for full IR process see SEC-IR-Playbook (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
 - Keep evidence exports out of ephemeral endpoints. Avoid Slack for transferring raw evidence files; use secure evidence buckets and Confluence links to manifests only.

Open questions / TODOs:
 - Add encrypted, HSM-backed evidence storage for high-risk incidents.
 - Define retention exceptions workflow for legal holds.
 - Complete script to automatically compute diffs between IAM snapshots and attach to manifest.
